{{Quote|. . . a Plex-fired GAM is the best seek-and-destroy weapon I've seen for use against repulsorcraft. It's fast, and almost impossible to shake once it locks onto a target. I admit the GAM's visual tracking system can be confused by other images in the sky. Good evasive maneuvers can lose the missile, too. But once it's caught a repulsor signature, that craft is gone.|Imperial [[Trooper/Legends|Trooper]] [[Reynol Kosk]]|<ref name="ISB" />}}
The '''Gravity-Activated Mode guided missile''' ("'''GAM'''") was a [[Guided missile/Legends|guided missile]] developed by [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions]] for use with their [[PLX-2M portable missile launcher]]. It possessed two tracking modes, selected at the push of a firing stud on the [[Missile launcher/Legends|missile launcher]]: EPR mode, which locked onto high-level [[Infrared/Legends|infrared]] sources such as vehicular or missile exhausts, and the namesake GAM mode, which first tracks a target's silhouette until close enough to home in on the [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]]-wave anomalies resulting from an active [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]]. The silhouette-tracking system could be evaded by careful maneuvering or confused by other objects above the horizon, but it was extremely unlikely to lose its target once close enough to acquire a repulsor signature. The missile was capable of pursuing its target for forty [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] before expending its fuel.<ref name="ISB" />

In addition to the PLX-2, GAM missiles could also be used by the [[PLX-4 Missile Launcher]]<ref name="TTSB">''[[The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref> and the [[LX-80]] anti-[[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] missile emplacement. They cost 600 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="H&S">''[[Hideouts & Strongholds]]''</ref>
